A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, with Tensor-GaLore extended and renamed TensorGRaD. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching retained experiments and proofs across relocation and renaming.

before.justification: V1 reports original FNO training experiments on Burgers, Darcy flow, Navier–Stokes and electromagnetic propagation, including accuracy, memory, rank ablations and execution times.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds high-Reynolds-number Navier–Stokes results, sparse/low-rank comparisons, precision experiments and additional ablations.

M1.justification: V1 uses Tucker-based low-rank gradient projection. V2 Algorithm 1 adds an unstructured sparse branch, compresses the residual with the low-rank branch, maintains separate Adam moments and combines their updates with scaling parameters. The earlier method remains as the low-rank-only component; the hybrid is a substantive procedural extension.

E1.justification: V2 adds highly turbulent Kolmogorov flow, described at approximately Re = 2×10^5 in Appendix A and labeled 10^5 in the main results. V1's Re = 10^3 Navier–Stokes data and the other PDE datasets remain. This substantially extends the dynamical regime tested; 1024×1024 resolution itself was already present in v1.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's uncompressed and matrix-GaLore comparisons, v2 evaluates GRASS-inspired structured-sparse tensor methods, including top-k, probability and random selection, and a randomized-SVD low-rank variant. The earlier tensor method becomes an explicit low-rank-only control for the hybrid method. These comparators appear in reported results, especially Tables 1–4 and 11.

E3.justification: V2 introduces full, Mixed-1 and Mixed-2 precision controls, sparse-density and composition experiments, and a new high-Re evaluation protocol. Appendix A specifies 1,577 training and 279 test pairs with temporal offset 256 and stride 4; Table 13 specifies a staged 256-to-1024 training schedule. These are new experimental settings, not evidence that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 retains earlier rank, matricization and timing analyses while adding gradient-reconstruction error distributions, sparse-versus-low-rank ordering and residual/additive comparisons, precision sensitivity, projection-update frequency and sparse-mask selection ablations. Figures 3 and 7 and Tables 2, 3 and 11 test substantial new questions about the hybrid method's behavior.

E5.justification: V1 Table 6 already contains ± values without specifying their interpretation or run count. V2 Tables 1 and 4 explicitly report means ± one standard error over three seeds, and Appendix F discloses three profiling repeats. Reporting remains uneven: Table 11 promises standard deviations but displays only point estimates. No increase in runs for retained results is established.

E6.justification: Earlier benchmark values are retained under Tensor low-rank labels in v2 Tables 5–10 and 12. Substantial new results include high-Re test L2 values of 16.82±0.18 for full-precision TensorGRaD versus 17.02±0.18 for Adam, both ×10^-2 (Table 1), and precision-dependent degradation in Table 3. These are newly reported conditions and findings, not same-setting improvements over v1's Navier–Stokes scores.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions of sparse supports, structured Cartesian-product masks and projection/back-projection operations in Section 2.2 and Appendix E. The principal stable-rank, FNO-reversibility and fixed-projection convergence results remain essentially unchanged across v1 Appendices H–J and v2 Appendices K–M. No corresponding new convergence proof for the full hybrid update is supplied.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on structure-preserving low-rank tensor-gradient compression and optimizer-memory savings up to 75%. V2 makes combined sparse-plus-low-rank compression and a mixed-precision recipe central contributions, emphasizing highly turbulent PDE evaluation and total-memory savings exceeding 50%. This substantially redefines the claimed contribution and its supporting scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking sparse entries to localized outliers, low-rank factors to global structure, and sparse-first ordering to improved factor estimation. It also interprets update-frequency effects and half-precision optimizer degradation. Beyond v1's decomposition-overhead and rank-selection limitations, v2 discusses sparse-index costs, joint rank/sparsity selection and the need for full-precision optimizer states.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation and reproducibility information: COO storage and scatter reconstruction, precision allocation, dataset-pair construction, decomposition-update frequencies, detailed NS1024 training configurations, and A100/H100/H200 hardware. Appendix F adds profiling warmup, collection and allocation-classification details. The stated code location changes from an anonymous repository to the named TensorGRaD repository.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around GRASS, robust PCA, robust tensor decomposition and low-rank-plus-sparse recovery. It also distinguishes gradient compression from SLTrain's weight decomposition and Scatterbrain's attention decomposition. V1 primarily positioned its contribution against matrix GaLore and tensor-weight compression; several earlier citations and their associated discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and results narrative are extensively rewritten around TensorGRaD. Setup and results are combined, substantial background and dataset descriptions move to appendices, and standalone implicit-regularization and applications sections disappear. Explicit limitations and broader-impact passages are added. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the method's renaming.

P2.justification: V2 adds a hybrid-method schematic, reconstruction-error plots, turbulent-flow snapshots and new precision/composition tables, while redesigning the main memory–accuracy displays. Existing material is also relocated: v1 Figure 2 becomes v2 Figure 8, and v1 Table 1 becomes v2 Table 6. Typography, spacing and table placement change substantially throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through sparse and low-rank controls, precision and composition ablations, a harder turbulent benchmark, explicit three-seed uncertainty and fuller reproduction details. These make the memory–accuracy trade-off considerably more assessable than in v1. Important qualifications remain: Table 1's 52-to-29 GB reduction is approximately 44%, despite the accompanying 55% claim, and the retained proofs address the low-rank component rather than the full hybrid method. These shortcomings limit the headline claims but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
